channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Tasweer Residency 2026–2027: As the Image Unfolds
item.description: The second edition of the residency from Tasweer, Qatar's photo festival organised by Qatar Museums. Three emerging photographers and visual storytellers based in Qatar, aged 21+, are selected for a five-month residency (1 October 2026 – 1 March 2027) at Bayt Al Wakrah in historic Old Al Wakrah City. Built around the concept of 'athar' — an Arabic word for traces, imprints and legacies — residents develop a project across documentary, conceptual, or experimental image-making. Each receives studio space at Bayt Al Wakrah, mentorship and professional development, access to local networks, and a monthly stipend of 4,000 QAR. Completed projects are presented in the exhibition 'As the Image Unfolds — The Language of Athar' during the 2027 Tasweer Photo Festival, accompanied by an online zine documenting the process. Apply with a cover letter, artist bio and statement, CV, a 15–20 image portfolio (PDF), a residency statement of intent, and 1–2 recommendation letters. Free to apply. — Deadline: September 3, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 4,000 QAR/month stipend + exhibition.

item.title: The Soldier's Lens 2026 · Florida Museum of Photographic Arts
item.description: FMoPA's second annual curated exhibition honoring military life, open to active-duty service members, veterans, and immediate family members. Free to submit up to 3 photographs capturing lived experience in and around military service; a panel versed in art and military service selects the show. Selected works are exhibited at FMoPA in Tampa November 5, 2026 – January 10, 2027, timed with Veterans Day, and featured in the museum's online gallery. All ages welcome (under-18s with parental consent). — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Museum exhibition.

item.title: Hand Fetish Projects — Issue #01: How to Survive in Southeast Asia
item.description: Founding print issue from independent arthouse Hand Fetish Projects, collecting images made from within Southeast Asia — humidity, density, informal architecture, urban exhaustion — alongside outside encounters with the region. Illustration, photography and mixed-media work is welcome, with experimental and analogue approaches encouraged; submit up to 3 works with a short artist statement. Selected artists receive the print-ready PDF edition free, physical copies at production cost, full copyright retained, and credit in the HFP archive. Publication expected September 2026. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: Delfina Foundation — Mondriaan Fund Netherlands Residency 2027
item.description: Three-month residency at Delfina Foundation in London (September 27 – December 17, 2027) for visual artists and curators who are Dutch or based in the Netherlands, organised in partnership with the Mondriaan Fund. Artists receive €9,188 and curators €7,232 toward travel, materials and living costs, with studio and accommodation paid directly to Delfina; residents contribute 10% personally. Apply in English via the Mondriaan Fund's digital application system. Deadline August 27, 2026, before 16:00 Dutch time. — Deadline: August 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency.

item.title: In Community: LACP's Annual Members' Exhibition
item.description: The Los Angeles Center of Photography's annual members' exhibition, open to current LACP members — membership can be purchased online before submitting. Juror Chandra Glick, Photo Director at Artforum, selects works for the show at LACP's downtown Los Angeles gallery, October 1–November 5, 2026, with an opening reception on October 1. Prizes: 1st place $500 cash; 2nd place $250 LACP gift card plus a one-year membership; 3rd place $250 LACP gift card; honorable mentions also awarded. Entry fees are tiered from $18.75 for a single image to $150 for 31–35 images. Images and texts created by AI are not accepted. — Deadline: August 11, 2026. Fee: $18.75–$150. Prize: $500 cash + exhibition.

item.title: Dek Unu Magazine — November 2026 Issue
item.description: International not-for-profit journal publishing one accomplished artist per monthly issue in print and online paperback. All fine art projects in all photo genres and techniques are welcome — each feature pairs 11 images with per-image commentary and an in-depth interview. Technical excellence paired with artistic vision and conceptual intent. Submission window for the November issue runs September 1–20, 2026; email submissions. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Photo Trouvée Magazine Issue 21 — Garden of Nostalgia
item.description: Print Issue 21 open call themed 'Garden of Nostalgia' for artists who work with or are inspired by vintage found or family photographs — florals, plants, connections to nature, or reflections on roots. Any media accepted. Selected artists receive a designated page spread with artist statement, a complimentary digital issue, and website, newsletter and social media features. The $40 publishing fee (due late October if selected) funds printing, design and a scholarship fund. International submissions welcome. — Deadline: October 10, 2026. Fee: Free to submit; $40 if selected. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: SlowExposures 2026 — Book Fair
item.description: Showcase and sell your photography book during the SlowExposures festival weekend — Saturday, September 19, 1–3 PM at the historic R.F. Strickland Building in Concord, Georgia. Open to the first 10 photographers who register; in lieu of a fee each participant donates one book, featured in the festival's print raffle at the Saturday evening dinner. Participants present their work to a public audience, with promotion through the festival's channels. — Deadline: September 19, 2026. Fee: Free (donate one book). Prize: Festival exhibition.

item.title: Raghu Rai MA-g Awards for Photography 2026 · Museum of the Avant-garde
item.description: The Museum of Avant-garde's annual photography award, chaired in 2026 by the Raghu Rai Foundation in his honour following his passing. Open to all — professionals, students and enthusiasts — on any theme; winning and shortlisted works are selected for the Museum's contemporary collection and featured online and in future exhibitions. The MA-g Awards name each edition after its judges; past photography jurors include William Klein, Nobuyoshi Araki, Graciela Iturbide and Antanas Sutkus. Photography entry is €55 single / €110 series, with early-bird, student and low-income-country discounts. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: €55–110. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Monochrome · Aurea Photogallery
item.description: Aurea Photogallery's black-and-white open call, asking photographers to leave colour behind and work with light, shadow, shape and texture alone. Portraits, landscapes, quiet street work and abstract shadows are all welcome, with an emphasis on strong contrast and raw emotion. Selected work runs in a one-month online exhibition (18 August – 14 September 2026) with a PDF and print-on-demand catalogue, a dedicated artist page and permanent inclusion in the gallery's archive. Submissions are reviewed on a rolling basis. — Deadline: August 12, 2026. Fee: Free (€30 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + Catalog.

item.title: 2027 Small Stones Festival of the Arts
item.description: Eighth edition of the juried festival run jointly by the Worcester County Camera Club and the Blackstone Valley Art Association, held in a restored barn outside Worcester. Fine art photography is judged as its own category — film, digital, infrared and alternative processes all eligible — with its own jurors and prizes, alongside fine art painting. 144 works are selected for the in-person exhibition and printed in a hardbound catalogue; all entries appear in the online Web Gallery. Work must be hand-delivered, and framed pieces are capped at 26 inches on the longest edge. The art call opens 1 September 2026. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: $10/entry. Prize: Exhibition + Cash awards + Catalog.

item.title: Open Call for Exhibitions — Prospekto and Vilnius Photography Galleries
item.description: The Lithuanian Photographers' Association invites artists and curators to propose solo, group or curatorial photography exhibitions for its two Vilnius spaces — Prospekto Gallery on Gedimino Avenue and the Vilnius Photography Gallery. Applications are accepted year-round with no fixed deadline; selections are made once a year, in August. Submit an exhibition proposal of up to 500 words naming the preferred gallery and exhibition period, a bio of up to 100 words, and a portfolio with supporting visual material such as documentation of previous installations. Total submission size must not exceed 5 MB. Free to enter. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: Spotlight Awards 2026
item.description: Production Paradise's annual commercial and advertising photography awards, now in their ninth edition. The real draw is the jury: more than fifty picture editors, art buyers, creative directors and brand leads from IKEA, The Economist, Volvo Cars, Unilever, Louis Vuitton, Cartier, Ogilvy, Droga5, UNICEF, The Guardian and Mattel. Entrants opt in to having their work shown to every judge, and the organisers pitch it as a hiring channel as much as a competition — winner or not. Fifteen categories, one of them for AI-developed imagery. Each submission is a single image, commissioned or personal work, open to photographers in all countries over 18. The Grand Prize winner takes $1,000 cash plus a portfolio review ticket and strategy sessions; category winners receive sponsor packages, with a total prize pool over $40,000. Shortlists are announced from 1 September, winners on 22 September 2026. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: €35 first entry, €25 each additional. Prize: $1,000 + Portfolio review.

item.title: Global Reporting Grants
item.description: The Pulitzer Center's open, catch-all reporting grant — no restriction on topic or region — funding in-depth journalism on systemic issues that get too little coverage. Photographers are explicitly eligible alongside reporters, audio and video journalists and documentary filmmakers; staff and freelancers of any nationality can apply. Grants cover reporting costs against a reasonable, detailed budget; most awards for international travel fall between $5,000 and $10,000. It does not fund staff salaries, equipment purchases, books, feature-length films, routine breaking news or data projects aimed solely at academic research. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with no deadline; half the grant is paid once paperwork is complete and the remainder on submission of the finished work. Grantees join the Center's reporting network and its education and outreach programs. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000–$10,000.

item.title: Sum Sum Summ-A-Time · Drawing Rooms
item.description: Drawing Rooms, a nonprofit art space in Jersey City, gathers work about summertime for an online-only show on Artsy — scenes and places, summer food, leisure, flora and fauna, and the colours and sensations of the season. Photography sits alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, collage, fibre and sculpture, with no size limitation and no AI-generated or reproduced work accepted. Three images are covered by the entry fee and further images may be added for $5 each. The exhibition runs August 6–30, 2026 on Artsy.net, with exhibited work offered for sale at a 60/40 split in the artist's favour. — Deadline: July 22, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Solo Project Space #8 · Drawing Rooms
item.description: Drawing Rooms hands over its Project Space and up to four further gallery areas to artists with a cohesive body of work or an installation — any theme, any concept, any size or medium, photography included. One artist takes the main Project Space and up to four more are given solo areas in the Jersey City galleries for the autumn slot, September 10 – October 11, 2026, with an opening reception on September 12 and a closing reception on October 11. Selected artists may also be picked up for other Drawing Rooms programmes, including The Art Project and the gallery's Artsy.net exhibits. Work must be original and available for sale, with 60% of proceeds to the artist. — Deadline: August 11, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: 10th SIPF Photo Market 2026 — Call for Exhibitors
item.description: The Singapore International Photography Festival opens its Photo Market to publishers, artists, collectives and creatives who want to show and sell photobooks, self-published zines, journals, prints, art objects and photography merchandise. The market runs across the opening weekend of the 10th SIPF biennale, October 17–18, 2026, within walking distance of the festival's main exhibition venues and free for the public to enter. Booths include a table and two chairs for up to two people, with a reduced Young Creatives rate for current students and graduates of the past three years; a hardship option can be flagged in the form. The market is curated and applications are assessed on a rolling basis, with no payment due until an application is successful. — Deadline: August 7, 2026. Fee: SGD 120–200. Prize: Exhibition booth.

item.title: Anthology Cover Art Competition 2026
item.description: Anthology, an Irish print magazine covering art, interiors, travel and literature, runs this competition to find the image for a future cover. Photography is judged alongside painting, printmaking, mixed media and digital work by an independent panel, so the winning image has to hold a whole cover on its own terms. The winner receives €500, the cover itself, and editorial coverage in print and online. Single images only, with unlimited separate entries; work already used on another publication's cover is ineligible, as is anything made with generative AI. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: €18. Prize: €500 + Publication.

item.title: A Show of Heads 2026 · Limner Gallery
item.description: SlowArt Productions' long-running annual exhibition at Limner Gallery in Hudson, New York, devoted to every reading of the human head — traditional portraiture, abstraction, caricature, the conceptual and the surreal. Photography sits alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, graphics, digital work, video and installation, with wall pieces up to 72 by 120 inches. Four works are covered by the entry fee and further works cost $5 each. Accepted artists pay nothing further: the show runs October 8–31, 2026 in the gallery and online, with a 35% commission on sales at prices the artist sets. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Guest Room: Whitney Hubbs & Jermaine Francis · Der Greif
item.description: The latest edition of Der Greif's monthly curator-led open call, guest-curated by artists Whitney Hubbs and Jermaine Francis. The brief asks for work exploring the materiality of photography and its spatial possibilities — an invitation to treat the photograph as an object and a situation rather than a window. Up to five images per project may be submitted, along with video up to ten minutes. Selected work is featured in Der Greif's online showcase, and selected artists also receive an online portfolio review with the curators. Submission is through Picter and the fee is genuinely voluntary — enter for free or donate €5 or €10. — Deadline: August 17, 2026. Fee: Free (optional €5 or €10 donation). Prize: Publication.

item.title: Preserving the Spirit · artCentral
item.description: A juried photography exhibition marking the 100th anniversary of Route 66, presented by artCentral in Carthage, Missouri — itself a Route 66 town. The call invites photographers to capture the highway in all its forms: neon-lit motels, vintage gas stations, vast landscapes, small-town main streets and the people who embody the road's enduring character. Creative edits are allowed, but work must be photographic, Route 66 inspired, framed and wired for hanging, and available for sale. Open to photographers 18 and over nationwide; up to three works may be submitted for jury consideration. The exhibition runs September 25 – October 30, 2026. — Deadline: September 5, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Space Between Is What Remains · Rolo Gallery
item.description: A national juried exhibition at Rolo Gallery, a contemporary space that opened in May 2026 on Denver's Art District on Santa Fe. The call asks for work that holds something — a mark, a quality of light, a feeling that doesn't leave — and is deliberately loose about interpretation: abstract, figurative or anywhere between, with no requirement that work announce its connection to the theme. Photography is welcome alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, mixed media, fibre, ceramics, works on paper and book arts. Open to US-based artists 18 and over at all career stages, with no exhibition history required. The show runs September 3 – October 11, 2026, spanning two First Friday art walks and a Third Friday reception on September 19. — Deadline: July 30, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Beyond The Surface: Exploring Above and Below · Hera Gallery
item.description: Hera Gallery — an artist-run cooperative in Wakefield, Rhode Island, founded in 1974 — invites work that makes the invisible visible, navigating the space between inner and outer worlds, the terrestrial and the cosmic. Seen from space, earth is a small blue dot where boundaries dissolve; the call asks where each artist's work sits within that spectrum, whether through a personal, public, spiritual or cosmic lens. All media welcome, 2D, 3D and video. Juror Lydia Jasper is Assistant Curator at MASS MoCA. Submission fees run on a sliding scale, honour system; the gallery takes no commission, so 100% of sales go to the artist. Exhibition runs October 17 – November 14, 2026. — Deadline: August 15, 2026. Fee: $35 (sliding scale). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Artist in Residence 2027 · Center for the Arts Evergreen
item.description: Twelve-week residencies in the foothills west of Denver, offered three times across 2027 (February 1 – April 30, May 10 – August 6, and August 16 – November 12). Residents get housing in a private one-bedroom cottage, a private studio with 24-hour secure access, paid teaching and workshop opportunities, exhibition space, an artist page on the CAE website and a $250 monthly stipend paid on completion ($750 total), plus chances to sell work at CAE events. In return each artist develops and facilitates one community programme tied to their residency plan. Open to artists 18 and over living and working in the US; photography, film, video, new media and interdisciplinary practice are all eligible, though digital artists must bring their own equipment. — Deadline: October 2, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Residency + $750 stipend.

item.title: Torn · Drawing Rooms
item.description: Drawing Rooms, a nonprofit art space in Jersey City, wants to expand what the word 'torn' can mean. The show seeks work that results wholly or partly from the act of tearing — collage, fibre, painting, assemblage — or that documents the residue of that act, a photograph of what tearing left behind, or that composes competing elements and narratives which refuse to resolve. Photography, prints, drawing, painting and sculpture are all accepted; AI-generated and reproduced works are not. Up to three unframed images may be submitted. Exhibited work must be for sale, split 60/40 in the artist's favour. The exhibition runs September 10 – October 11, 2026, with notification on August 16. — Deadline: August 11, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Galleries in City of Auburn
item.description: The City of Auburn, Washington is seeking artists and artist groups working in two-dimensional or small three-dimensional media for eight-week exhibitions in its city-operated gallery spaces during 2027, including the Cheryl Sallee Gallery at the Auburn Senior Activity Center — fitted with an Arakawa hanging system and professional gallery lighting — and the Community & Event Center. Photography is explicitly among the media invited, alongside printmaking, painting, drawing, mixed media, textiles, mosaic, glass, collage, fibre art, ceramics and metal sculpture. Shows run roughly 5–12 works. There is no entry fee and no location restriction, but selected artists must deliver and collect work in person in Auburn. — Deadline: September 2, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Many Countries in One · Artspiration Frederick
item.description: A celebration of immigrant artists who enrich the cultural fabric of the United States, hosted by Artspiration Frederick, a nonprofit art organisation and community artist space in Frederick, Maryland. Artists born outside the US and now living in the continental US are invited to submit original work in any visual medium — photography, painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, fibre art, ceramics, mixed media and digital art among them — reflecting their own voice and experience. Cuban-American artist, curator and critic F. Lennox Campello serves as juror and curator. Up to three works may be entered; 2D work must be framed and wired. The exhibition runs January 1–31, 2027 in the Artspiration Frederick Gallery. — Deadline: December 11, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Winter 2027 'Vintage' Issue · Penn Journal of Arts and Sciences
item.description: The Penn Journal of Arts and Sciences is an independent publication founded in 2024 that presents contemporary creative work across disciplines, with a primary focus on visual art and poetry alongside experimental and cross-disciplinary practice. Submissions made before this deadline are considered for the Winter 2027 'Vintage' issue, published both online and in print within the journal's curated editorial framework. Selected contributors may also be included in editorial features, interviews and wider PJAS releases. The call is open internationally to artists and writers at all career stages, working in any discipline, with individual and collaborative submissions accepted. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: $14. Prize: Publication.

item.title: ALT · Photo Opp
item.description: Juried show at Photo Opp, a nonprofit community darkroom and visual workspace housed in the former Moses Montefiore Synagogue in downtown Appleton, Wisconsin. ALT celebrates photography as a medium without limits and asks what happens when artists step outside the expected: cyanotypes and salt prints, film soup, unconventional printing surfaces, digital manipulation, sculptural photography, emulsion lifting, collage and anything that challenges convention or expands the definition of a photograph. The brief prizes curiosity over perfection, process over predictability, risk over routine. Open to Wisconsin residents (work may have been made anywhere, anytime); up to three pieces per artist, free to enter. Selected work hangs in the Community Gallery from October 2026, with an opening reception and awards announcement on October 16, and is featured in a promotional zine sold as a fundraiser. The gallery takes no commission on sales. — Deadline: August 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Zine publication.

item.title: This Land Is Your Land · Library Arts Center
item.description: Community photography exhibit at the Library Arts Center gallery in Newport, New Hampshire, marking America's 250th anniversary. The call asks photographers to share images of the places, faces, traditions and stories that make up the fabric of America — sweeping landscapes and quiet hometown streets, everyday moments and the people who shape communities, natural beauty alongside resilience and heritage. Open to photographers of all experience levels who live in New Hampshire or Vermont, or who have a distinct connection to the area; up to two pieces per photographer. Entry is free for Library Arts Center members and $5 otherwise. Accepted artists are notified by July 28 and deliver framed, ready-to-hang work to the gallery on August 5–6. The exhibit runs August 15 – October 9, 2026, with an opening reception on August 14. — Deadline: July 23, 2026. Fee: $5 (free for members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Current Works 2026 · Kansas City Society for Contemporary Photography
item.description: The annual juried exhibition of the Kansas City Society for Contemporary Photography, a long-running nonprofit devoted to contemporary photographic practice in the Midwest. Current Works sets out to show what photographic artists are doing now, and the call explicitly welcomes a broad range of styles and processes — digital, film, alternative process, black and white or colour — representing the diversity of photographic excellence in the region. Open to residents of Missouri, Kansas, Iowa, Nebraska, Arkansas, Oklahoma and Texas; work must have been produced between 2024 and 2026 and be built on the entrant's own original photography, with no AI-generated imagery. KCSCP members receive 20% off the entry fee, and students can request a discount code. The 2026 juror is John W. Hans, a Kansas City photographer of nearly fifty years and Director of Production at Dolphin Archival Printing inside Haw Contemporary, whose own abstract, landscape-rooted work is held in the H&R Block and Kansas City International Airport collections. Selected work is exhibited November 12 – December 31, 2026. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: $50 (up to 5 images; 20% off for members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Proximity of Harm — Visions of a Compromised Everyday Life · Fondazione Ippocrate
item.description: First edition of an international photography competition run by the Ippocrate Foundation, an independent Italian organisation working on health, environment and social transformation, as part of a cultural research project into contemporary forms of harm. The brief treats harm in an extended, layered sense — not only environmental damage but a diffuse condition running through relationships, social systems and the construction of individual and collective identity, and equally emotional and perceptual. The project positions photography as a tool of critical observation, looking for personal ways of seeing what is close and everyday yet stays invisible; the aim is not to document harm didactically but to offer an authentic, contemporary perspective. Open to photographers, artists and authors of any nationality aged 18 or over; one to three images, as single pictures or a coherent series, no AI-generated work. The jury is chaired by World Press Photo winner Pablo Ernesto Piovano and includes photographers Pierpaolo Mittica, Ilaria Di Biagio and Ilenia Baldina, and director Silvia Chiodin. Selected photographs are screened on September 18 at Palazzetto Widmann during the Ippocrate Convention in Bagnoli di Sopra, and the three winners are invited to a masterclass with Piovano at the Teatro Carlo Goldoni on September 19 (travel and accommodation at the participant's own expense). — Deadline: August 15, 2026. Fee: €10. Prize: Exhibition screening & masterclass with Piovano.

item.title: TWISTED 2026 · Cape Cod Art Center
item.description: Cape Cod Art Center's autumn online juried exhibit for digital art — including digital photography, composites, and digitally manipulated imagery that twists, distorts, or reimagines the familiar. Open to all; up to five pieces may be submitted with a maximum of two accepted. Selected work appears in the online juried exhibition with awards and promotion through the gallery's channels. — Deadline: October 25, 2026. Fee: $15/piece. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Shape of a Life · Decagon Gallery
item.description: Online juried photography exhibition from Decagon Gallery on the idea that a life is not defined by its milestones alone. The brief welcomes portraits, landscapes, interiors, gestures, and quiet everyday moments that reveal human experience with honesty and depth rather than surface description. Selected work is shown in a curated online exhibition with dedicated pages and published in a professionally designed exhibition catalog, alongside digital badges and certificates. Open to photographers worldwide; up to 4 images. First place receives $500, second $250, third $150, and two honorable mentions $50 each — $1,000 total in cash awards — plus a Human Presence Award granting free entry to a future exhibition. — Deadline: October 10, 2026. Fee: $25 (4 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $1,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Mythus: A National Exhibit of Folklore Inspired Artworks
item.description: National juried exhibition at d'Art Center, the nonprofit art center in Norfolk, Virginia's NEON District (est. 1986), for artworks inspired by folklore — the stories, legends, myths, fairy tales, folktales, rituals and traditions of cultures from around the world. All mediums welcome, including photography, 2D or 3D; 3 to 10 works. Exhibition in the gallery September 26 – October 24, 2026. — Deadline: August 9, 2026. Fee: $30 (3 works), $5 each additional. Prize: $300 + Exhibition.

item.title: New Emergence Art Prize 2026
item.description: An international online art prize for emerging artists working in any medium, including photography, founded by artist Habib Hajallie RBA. With a prize fund of over £5,000, the 2026 edition awards a £1,000 grand prize alongside a two-week NG Art Creative Residency in Provence, France, a year on Parker Harris's Art Ladder mentoring programme, and several materials awards. The judging panel includes Addi Aegisdottir, Creative Director of the Mall Galleries. Open to artists worldwide with no set theme; up to three works may be submitted and selected work is presented online. Deadline 3 August 2026. — Deadline: August 3, 2026. Fee: £15–£30. Prize: £1,000 + Residency + Mentoring.

item.title: Call for Proposals for Solo Exhibitions · CSU Spur
item.description: CSU Spur, the Colorado State University System's public-facing campus at Denver's National Western Center, invites solo exhibition proposals for 2026–2027 celebrating the intersection of community, sustainability and innovation. Work exploring environmental stewardship, scientific curiosity and local storytelling is sought, with proposals around food, water and health especially encouraged. Open to artists of all experience levels working in any medium including photography; the galleries are public campus spaces. Submissions are reviewed quarterly on a rolling basis until the call closes November 1, 2026, with exhibition dates set in collaboration with campus staff. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: Solo/Group Show 2027 · Gallery 40
item.description: Gallery 40, the contemporary gallery at 40 Cannon Street in Poughkeepsie, is selecting artists for its 2027 solo and small-group exhibition program. Chosen artists — solo or in curated groups of up to four — receive a six-week show from February 6 to March 14, 2027 with an opening reception, and may be considered for artist talks, panel discussions or recorded interviews. All 2-dimensional work is considered, explicitly including photography; work must be for sale (40% commission), no larger than 48 x 48 inches framed, ready to hang, and not previously exhibited at the gallery. Open to US artists 18 and over; submissions are evaluated by the gallery's curators. — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: $40 (up to 10 images). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: IN SERIES · Art Fluent
item.description: Art Fluent's open call for a cohesive body of work — five pieces built around a single idea, shown as a mini solo show within a larger online group exhibition. Open to all fine art media including photography, worldwide, amateur and professional. Each accepted artist receives a $250 cash prize and a place in the online gallery at art-fluent.com. Curated by Creative Director Amy Matteson Neill and an anonymous committee; deadline October 9, 2026 (midnight MST), notification November 6. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: $35 for a series of 5. Prize: $250 per accepted artist.

item.title: Photography+ Open Call: Un/Stable — Lands, Anxieties, Dreams · Photoworks
item.description: Open call for the next issue of Photography+, Photoworks' online magazine, on the theme 'Un/Stable: Lands, Anxieties, Dreams' — work responding to the fragile, shifting conditions shaping our lives, environments, and collective futures, from displacement and ecological change to anxiety, resilience, care, and adaptation, and how photography can hold space for possibility. Submit a single image responding to the theme; one selected work receives an £80 artist fee and is featured in the upcoming issue of Photography+. Open to anyone, anywhere in the world, with no professional experience required. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £80 + Publication.

item.title: (S)Light of Hand 2026 · The Photographer's Eye Collective
item.description: The Photographer's Eye Collective's annual juried celebration of alternative, historical, and experimental photographic processes, staged at its nonprofit gallery on Grand Avenue in Escondido, California. Handmade, photo-based work is welcome — from albumen and cyanotype to ziatype, plus hand-worked digital or silver prints incorporating collage, stitching, or three-dimensional elements. The 2026 edition is juried by Ann M. Jastrab, Executive Director of the Center for Photographic Art in Carmel, with Juror's Choice and Director's Choice honors receiving an online exhibition and a printed catalog in 2027. Selected works are shown in the gallery 12 September – 31 October 2026, opening with a reception on 12 September. Open to photographers 18 and older; up to ten images per artist. — Deadline: August 7, 2026. Fee: $35 for 5 images; $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition + Catalog.

item.title: Animals 2026 · Grid Photo Gallery
item.description: International call from Grid Photo Gallery for work that engages with animal life in its many forms — wildlife, documentary, portraiture, fine art, conceptual, studio, and experimental photography are all welcome. Selection favours visual clarity, sensitivity of approach, and a strong awareness of form rather than any single genre. Selected work is shown in a curated online exhibition on the gallery site. First place is named Photographer of the Month with a profile interview, priority promotional placement, and a free entry in the next open call; second and third places are highlighted in the virtual exhibition. All selected entries receive permanent online display, social media promotion, a digital certificate, and a profile page linking to the photographer's site. The exhibition opens 1 September 2026. — Deadline: August 15, 2026. Fee: €7. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Head On Photo Awards 2026
item.description: The flagship international awards of Sydney's Head On Photo Festival, judged completely anonymously — jurors see the photograph, never the photographer's name, CV or following. Three categories: Portrait, Landscape and Exposure (anything that is not portrait or landscape), sharing an AUD 80,000 prize pool that includes AUD 5,000 cash for each category winner plus OM System camera kits. Around 40 finalists per category (20–30 for Exposure) are exhibited in print and online during the festival, 6–29 November 2026. Open internationally to photographers at every level, from phone snapshots to studio and documentary work. Entries are AUD 30 per image, half price for under-25s; final deadline 16 August 2026, 11:59pm Sydney time. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: $30 AUD per image; under-25s $15. Prize: AUD 80,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Prix LNP 2026 — Les Nuits Photo
item.description: The annual call for photographic films from Les Nuits Photo, the Paris festival devoted to the photo-film form, organised by the photographers' association Freelens in partnership with SAIF. Open internationally to all authors — established, emerging, students and amateurs alike, whether photographers, directors, editors, artists or journalists. The Grand Prix LNP carries a €1,000 award from SAIF plus diffusion on Fisheye Magazine and 9 Lives Magazine and screenings at partner festivals; the Prix LNP Diapéro, chosen by the Diapéro team, adds €500 and paid distribution on Mediapart. Submissions run 20 June – 15 September 2026 via Google Form; prizes are presented at the festival in Paris in November. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: Free (Freelens membership €15). Prize: €1,000 + Publication.

item.title: Bourse Transverse 2026 · Freelens / ADAGP
item.description: Joint grant from photographers' association Freelens and ADAGP, the French visual-arts authors' society, supporting a duo — a photographer and an artist from another visual discipline — in creating a work together and publishing it as a book. €12,000 in total: €7,000 to the winning duo and €5,000 towards the book's edition, with the work made within a year and the book published within two. Open to duos from the French scene (working or residing in France for at least five years, or French nationals living abroad) with professional track records of exhibitions or publications; a publisher may already be attached. Applications in French via the ADAGP candidature portal by 3 September 2026, 2pm; the winning duo is announced at Salon Polycopies in Paris on 12 November 2026. — Deadline: September 3, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €7,000 + Publication.

item.title: ABSURIA — International Abstract & Surrealist Photography Contest 2027
item.description: Second edition of the international festival dedicated exclusively to abstract and surrealist photography. Open to amateur and professional photographers worldwide. 100 photographs selected for physical exhibition across multiple venues in Tours, Loire Valley, France from May to September 2027, with all nominees also shown in 3D online galleries on the festival website. Fourteen winners honoured at the awards ceremony in Tours in early May 2027. Categories: Abstract Photography and Surrealist Photography, each with Professional and Amateur divisions plus a Young Hopefuls award; winners receive the ABSURIA Trophy, a gold statuette created for the contest. Fee tiered by number of works: amateur €20–€40, professional €25–€50, up to 6 works per registration with unlimited registrations. Images created solely with generative AI are excluded. — Deadline: April 30, 2027. Fee: €20–€50. Prize: Exhibition + trophy.

item.title: Booooooom x Format Creative Development Program
item.description: A free mentorship and portfolio development program from art platform Booooooom and portfolio-builder Format, aimed at visual artists, illustrators and photographers who are ready to grow rather than those with the most polished work. The grand prize recipient receives a lifetime Format subscription, personal mentorship with Booooooom editor-in-chief Jeff Hamada, and featured coverage on both platforms; two runners-up each receive a one-year Format plan and a portfolio review with Format's Stanzie Tooth. To apply, sign up for a free 60-day Format trial (no credit card required), build a portfolio of original work, and submit two short written statements — one describing the work, one on where you are in your practice and what support you're looking for. Open worldwide to artists 18+. Applications close September 2, 2026, 11:59pm PT. — Deadline: September 2, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Mentorship + Format subscription.

item.title: BWP x Nikon Grant Fund 2026 — Quarter 3 · Black Women Photographers
item.description: Third-quarter 2026 cycle of the Black Women Photographers x Nikon $50K Grant Fund — a year-long program supporting Black women photographers globally through four quarterly grant opportunities. The Q3 recipient receives a $2,500 USD unrestricted cash grant plus a Nikon Z6III with 24-70mm f/4 lens kit. Funding can support photography projects, production, travel, equipment, or other professional needs. BWP is a global membership community founded in 2020 by Polly Irungu, with members across 60+ countries and 35 U.S. states. Applications for Q3 close August 16, 2026; a final Q4 cycle follows later in the year. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $2,500 + Nikon Z6III kit.

item.title: Outdoor Photography Magazine — Summer Woodland
item.description: Submit up to 5 summer woodland images with captions for the 'One Thing This Month' feature (OP 332) in Outdoor Photography Magazine (UK). Winner receives a Vanguard VEO 3 303AB aluminium tripod (RRP £250). Captions up to 75 words with technical details (camera, lens, focal length, ISO, shutter speed, aperture). Entries upload via Google Form. — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Vanguard tripod (£250) + Publication.

item.title: Photobook Dummy Exhibition — 16th Lisbon Photobook Fair
item.description: Open call for the photobook dummy exhibition of the 16th Feira do Livro de Fotografia de Lisboa, held November 27–29, 2026 at the Arquivo Municipal de Lisboa – Fotográfico. Dummies are displayed for consultation throughout the fair, where past editions (72 projects by 65 authors in 2026) have drawn the attention of attending publishers and booksellers — a real chance to move a book project forward. Pre-register with up to 6 photographs of the dummy (72 dpi, max 2 MB each) via the Google Form by October 12, 21:00 GMT; confirmations October 23, dummies delivered by November 16. Participation is free. The fair also runs parallel calls for self-publisher/small-press tables and presentations of authorial projects. — Deadline: October 12, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.
